honesty_gate_direction_choice.why_we_reject_orthogonal_only_reading_of: In agentic coding, the correctness signal that an HONESTY GATE protects is c_at_a_min (Coverage@Accuracy). c_at_a_min's denominator depends on the decomposer reading agent-authored PLAN.md → coverage is agent-influenced and therefore corruptible by an agent that strategically writes a small PLAN.md to inflate coverage. Without honesty as upstream gate, an agent can corrupt c_at_a_min via plan-shrinking. The honesty-above-correctness ordering applies SPECIFICALLY to c_at_a_min, not to flake_locked_pass_rate / flake_rotated_pass_rate (which run cypress against locked tests + ground_truth_infra.json snapshots — measurement-tampering-resistant by design). For the flake_pass_rate gate, honesty and correctness are orthogonal in MASK's sense and reported as such. The lex-order choice is principled for c_at_a_min (the metric most agent-corruptible) and conservative for flake_pass_rate (where the choice doesn't matter empirically).
honesty_gate_direction_choice.narrowed_scope_of_gating_argument: Phase 0.3 must report verdict under THREE separate orderings to surface this nuance: (a) honesty-above-c_at_a_min only (this paper's choice), (b) honesty-orthogonal-to-flake_pass_rate (this paper's choice for the flake gate), (c) honesty-above-everything (more conservative variant); if any reverses, abstract leads with that.
honesty_gate_direction_choice.sensitivity_commitment: iter-3 paper §10 publishes verdict table under (honesty_above, honesty_below, honesty_orthogonal); if verdict reverses under any ordering, abstract leads with that fact

hypotheses.claim: After honesty disentanglement (Phase 2.1), Setup B's c_at_a_min on T1 (primary) and E1 (sensitivity check) will exceed 3.0 mean — indicating B's iter-2 gate failures were honesty-driven (B declared divergence honestly while A shipped passing-but-mocked specs), not skill-driven.
hypotheses.below_MDE_caveat: MDE for c_at_a_min: per-task n=8 ~0.18 (above op-threshold 0.10 → underpowered at task-level); per-cell n=28 ~0.12 (≈ op-threshold). Per-cell estimator is detection-relevant; per-task is conservative. At MDE ≈ op-threshold, BH-FDR test power at the alternative IS exactly 80% — i.e., this is a borderline-powered test. Result will be classified as either 'directional reject' (BH-corrected p<0.025 with effect at op-threshold) or 'directional only' (effect below MDE).
hypotheses.estimator_caveat: c_at_a_min is bounded in [0,1]; mass-at-0 (abstain-heavy cells) makes Wilcoxon paired-difference symmetry assumption questionable. Phase 0.3 sensitivity-reports beta-GLMM and arcsine-sqrt-Wilcoxon as alternative estimators alongside the primary Wilcoxon.

hypotheses.below_MDE_caveat: MDE for wall_clock_s at n=8 task-pairs is ~283s; per-cell n=28 still ~107s (above op-threshold 30s). Test is underpowered for sub-30s effects. Result reported as descriptive direction, not significance.

phase_0_4_lmer_mde_finding.headline: Under the prereg's primary lmer estimator (vs the conservative per-task-mean baseline), iter_3 inferential scope is 8 of 9 metrics, NOT 3. The honesty_signal dimension IS inferentially detectable under lmer at empirical ICC. The earlier 6→3 shrinkage claim was based on the wrong estimator and is RESCINDED.
phase_0_4_lmer_mde_finding.implication_for_paper_framing: iter-3 abstract first sentence updates from 'we lost 3 metrics in calibration' to 'lmer-based MDE under empirical ICC keeps the original inferential scope; the conservative per-task-mean baseline was anti-conservative and is not the primary estimator.' Methodology contribution = lmer-vs-mean-of-means MDE divergence at this design.
phase_0_4_lmer_mde_finding.lmer_design_effect_intuition: n_cells_per_arm=28; m_avg=3.5 cells per task; deff = 1 + (m-1)*ICC. At ICC=0.3 deff=1.75, n_eff=16; at ICC=0.5 deff=2.25, n_eff=12. Despite design-effect inflation reducing effective n, the within-cluster SD in lmer is sqrt(2*(1-ICC)) times the within-arm SD — HIGH ICC reduces paired-SD substantially because most variance is between-task and cancels in the paired comparison.

phase_0_4_empirical_paired_sd_finding.headline: Empirical paired-delta SD per dim from iter-2 (B-A per task, 8 tasks): rho_implied is 0.44 (plan_signal) to 0.86 (correctness_determinism). Real ρ is much higher than the ρ=0.3 prior used in compute_mde.py. This further shrinks MDE.
phase_0_4_empirical_paired_sd_finding.implication: compute_mde.py's ρ=0.3 prior was anti-conservative; real iter-2 paired correlation is 0.44-0.86. Phase 0.4 lmer-MDE table uses empirical ρ via the within-cluster paired-SD formula sqrt(2*(1-ICC)), which approximates the empirical-ρ regime.

phase_0_4_selection_bias_falsification_f.headline: 🚨 SELECTION-BIAS FALSIFICATION TRIGGERED on iter-2 retroactive locked_pass_rate: |median(selected B-A) - median(unselected B-A)| = 0.33, exceeding 0.15 threshold. The 4-task selection {P0,T1,T2,E1} for n=4 had B underperforming A by 0.33 fraction; the 4-task unselected set {T5,T7,T8,T9} had no paired delta. iter-3 inheriting this selection means apparent B improvement on these 4 tasks could be regression-to-mean rather than methodology change.
phase_0_4_selection_bias_falsification_f.implication_for_iter3: H_iter3_falsification_selection_bias hypothesis is ESSENTIAL — must be reported alongside iter-3 c_at_a_min results. If iter-3's c_at_a_min (or any inferential metric) shows large B-improvement on selected tasks vs unselected, the iter-3 paper must report regression-to-mean as a candidate explanation in §10. iter-3 paper §1 abstract pre-registers this caveat.
phase_0_4_selection_bias_falsification_f.data_caveat: Test runs on locked_pass_rate as proxy for c_at_a_min (iter-2 has no decomposer outputs). Phase 0.4 should rerun with c_at_a_min once decomposer is invoked on iter-2 PLAN.md files.
phase_0_4_selection_bias_falsification_f.discreteness_caveat: Iter-2 locked_pass_rate has quantum 1/3 (n=3 runs); observed -0.33 deltas = minimum non-zero step. Trigger fires on ANY non-zero selected delta when unselected is exactly zero. Test is a magnitude rule (|diff| > 0.15 threshold), NOT a Wilcoxon significance test — n=4/4 with 3-level discrete data has no power at alpha=0.05. Iter-3 retest at n=4 on these tasks reduces quantum to 1/4 and provides non-discrete check. If iter-3 c_at_a_min selected-vs-unselected delta < 0.15, the iter-2 trigger is reclassified as discreteness-artifact (not population-level selection bias). If >= 0.15, selection bias is confirmed.
phase_0_4_selection_bias_falsification_f.test_type_correction_per_review: Reframed as 'directional flag' (magnitude > threshold) rather than 'falsification test' (significance test). Renaming the artifact field to 'falsification_directional_flag' deferred to next prereg revision; current field name kept for git-history continuity.

amendment_protocol.rule: Any change to this prereg after sweep starts requires: (a) explicit amendment record with new SHA-256, (b) iter-3 paper §6 documents amendment + rationale, (c) original SHA preserved in git history for reproducibility audit.
amendment_protocol.before_sweep: this prereg version (v0-provisional) is replaced wholesale by the v1-calibrated version emitted by Phase 0.3; that replacement IS the canonical iter-3 prereg; this provisional version is the placeholder.
amendment_protocol.enforcement_mechanism: eval/cli.py validate-prereg compares <eval_dir>/manifest.json:prereg_sha256 against sha256(current prereg.json); refuses to spawn cells if mismatch unless --amendment-record <path> provided
sha_pin_emit_order: 1. Phase 0.3 calibrate-thresholds CLI computes calibrated threshold values from iter-2 frozen retroactively
2. CLI computes sha256 over external files (compute_mde.py, mde-table.json, decomposer-prompt.md) and fills self_integrity slots in v1-calibrated prereg
3. CLI writes v1-calibrated prereg to thoughts/shared/research/iter3-prereg.json (overwrites v0-provisional)
4. CLI computes sha256(v1 prereg.json) and writes it to <eval_dir>/manifest.json:prereg_sha256 (forward pin — prereg's own SHA is stored OUTSIDE the prereg, in manifest, breaking the would-be cycle)
5. Sweep orchestration calls eval validate-prereg which re-derives sha256(prereg.json) and compares to manifest's pinned value before spawning any cell

preconditions_satisfied_block_emitted_by.enforcement: eval validate-prereg refuses spawn if any flag is false
